scenes.visual: Title card 'One Segment, Constant Volume' over a pink ringed earthworm half-buried in brown soil. Same world and COLOUR MAP as the first film: outer layer BLUE; mesoderm and muscle ORANGE; gut lining YELLOW; gut lumen WHITE; coelomic fluid PALE CYAN; septa drawn as thin ORANGE discs; setae as tiny dark bristles. All shapes are schematic cartoons labelled 'schematic'; no numbers on screen in this film.

scenes.tts: An earthworm has no bones. What does it push against to drive through soil? The first film showed that a body plan does not reveal ancestry. This film asks what a body plan is for.
scenes.visual: The earthworm pushes its front end into soil; a cartoon skeleton icon appears beside it and is crossed out. Brief inset: the first film's gene tree, which shrinks away as the camera returns to the worm.
scenes.narration: An earthworm has no bones. What does it push against to drive through soil? The first film showed that a body plan does not reveal ancestry. This film asks what a body plan is for.

scenes.tts: Zoom in on one segment of the earthworm. Its coelom holds fluid. Thin walls called septa largely separate it from the segments on either side.
scenes.visual: The camera dives into the worm's body; one ring becomes a cutaway cylinder of PALE CYAN fluid, with an ORANGE disc at each end labelled 'septum'. Neighbouring cylinders sit faintly on either side. The WHITE gut lumen in a YELLOW tube runs through the middle and through both septa; label 'gut, separate from the coelom'.
scenes.narration: Zoom in on one segment of the earthworm. Its coelom holds fluid. Thin walls called septa largely separate it from the segments on either side.

scenes.tts: Two muscle layers wrap the body wall. Circular muscles run around it, like rings. Longitudinal muscles run along the body.
scenes.visual: ORANGE hoops draw around the cylinder one by one, label 'circular muscle'. Then ORANGE strips draw lengthwise along the outside, running past the septa into the neighbouring segments, label 'longitudinal muscle'. A thin BLUE outer skin wraps everything.
scenes.narration: Two muscle layers wrap the body wall. Circular muscles run around it, like rings. Longitudinal muscles run along the body.

scenes.tts: Fluid cannot be squeezed into a smaller volume. So fluid held in by a muscular wall gives muscles something to push against. This is a hydrostatic skeleton, like water in a balloon. Here we treat one segment as sealed.
scenes.visual: A cartoon hand squeezes a water balloon: one end bulges as the middle narrows. The balloon morphs back into the PALE CYAN segment inside its ORANGE muscle wall; label 'hydrostatic skeleton = fluid + muscular wall'. A small tag on the segment, label 'model: one sealed segment'.
scenes.narration: Fluid cannot be squeezed into a smaller volume. So fluid held in by a muscular wall gives muscles something to push against. This is a hydrostatic skeleton, like water in a balloon. Here we treat one segment as sealed.

scenes.tts: The coelom does a second job. Organs inside it, such as the gut, can grow and move with some independence from the body wall.
scenes.visual: Cutaway segment: the YELLOW gut tube shifts relative to the PALE CYAN coelom while the BLUE and ORANGE body wall flexes around it; label 'organs can move somewhat independently of the wall'.
scenes.narration: The coelom does a second job. Organs inside it, such as the gut, can grow and move with some independence from the body wall.

scenes.tts: Now the circular muscles contract, and the segment gets narrower. The fluid has nowhere to go. Does the segment get longer, shorter, or stay the same?
scenes.visual: The ORANGE hoops tighten and glow; the cylinder's waist starts to narrow, then freezes mid-squeeze. Three answer cards: 'longer', 'shorter', 'same'.
scenes.narration: Now the circular muscles contract, and the segment gets narrower. The fluid has nowhere to go. Does the segment get longer, shorter, or stay the same?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Cards hold. A 5-second ring timer at bottom right.

scenes.tts: It gets longer. The volume must stay the same, so a narrower segment has to stretch. The septa move apart as the end faces shrink.
scenes.visual: The segment narrows and lengthens smoothly; both ORANGE septa slide outward. The circular end faces shrink. A label 'same volume' stays fixed on the cyan fluid. No numbers.
scenes.narration: It gets longer. The volume must stay the same, so a narrower segment has to stretch. The septa move apart as the end faces shrink.

scenes.tts: Now the longitudinal muscles contract. The segment gets shorter, so at the same volume it must get fatter. Tiny bristles called setae poke out and grip the soil.
scenes.visual: The lengthwise ORANGE strips glow and shorten; the septa slide together and the cylinder bulges wide. Dark bristles labelled 'setae' poke out from its sides into brown soil grains and hold.
scenes.narration: Now the longitudinal muscles contract. The segment gets shorter, so at the same volume it must get fatter. Tiny bristles called setae poke out and grip the soil.

scenes.tts: Because septa partition the coelom, neighbours can take different shapes. In textbook accounts, each segment works largely on its own. One is long and thin, reaching forward. Its neighbour is short, fat and anchored.
scenes.visual: Pull back to five segments in a row. One is long and thin, pushing forward; the one behind it is short and fat with setae out in the soil. Labels 'long, thin' and 'short, fat, anchored'.
scenes.narration: Because septa partition the coelom, neighbours can take different shapes. In textbook accounts, each segment works largely on its own. One is long and thin, reaching forward. Its neighbour is short, fat and anchored.

scenes.tts: Pass these shapes down the body as a wave. Long, thin segments reach ahead. Short, fat segments hold the ground behind them. And the worm moves forward through the soil.
scenes.visual: A wave of long-thin then short-fat segments travels from head to tail along the whole worm, looping twice; the worm advances past a marker pebble in the soil.
scenes.narration: Pass these shapes down the body as a wave. Long, thin segments reach ahead. Short, fat segments hold the ground behind them. And the worm moves forward through the soil.

scenes.tts: The same body plan has a second payoff. The gut runs through, from mouth to anus. Food moves one way, so successive regions can specialize in different jobs.
scenes.visual: The view becomes see-through: the YELLOW gut tube runs head to tail. Brown food particles enter at 'mouth' and move only rearward, an arrow labelled 'one way'.
scenes.narration: The same body plan has a second payoff. The gut runs through, from mouth to anus. Food moves one way, so successive regions can specialize in different jobs.

scenes.tts: A muscular pharynx takes food in. A crop stores it. A gizzard grinds it. A long intestine digests and absorbs it.
scenes.visual: Four gut regions light up in turn as named, each with a label and a tiny action: 'pharynx' pulsing as it sucks food in; 'crop' swelling with stored food; 'gizzard' squeezing grit; 'intestine', long, with particles breaking up and fading as they are digested and absorbed.
scenes.narration: A muscular pharynx takes food in. A crop stores it. A gizzard grinds it. A long intestine digests and absorbs it.

scenes.tts: So the earthworm needs no bones. Fluid held in by muscle is its skeleton. The volume stays the same. Narrow a segment, and it lengthens. Shorten it, and it widens.
scenes.visual: Back to one segment, alternating narrow-long and short-fat in a slow loop, with a fixed label 'same volume'. No other animals in frame.
scenes.narration: So the earthworm needs no bones. Fluid held in by muscle is its skeleton. The volume stays the same. Narrow a segment, and it lengthens. Shorten it, and it widens.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Line: 'At constant volume, a narrower segment is a longer one.'
